root_cause.text: The `epf_ntb_epc_cleanup` function in the pci-epf-vntb driver does not stop the delayed work `cmd_handler` before freeing the BAR mappings and doorbells that it accesses, leading to a use-after-free or invalid memory access when the work executes after resource teardown.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `disable_delayed_work_sync(&ntb->cmd_handler);` at the beginning of `epf_ntb_epc_cleanup`, with the commit message stating: "Disable the delayed work before clearing BAR mappings and doorbells to avoid running the handler after resources have been torn down." The attached Oops shows `epf_ntb_cmd_handler` accessing an invalid virtual address, confirming the race.

The attached Oops shows `epf_ntb_cmd_handler` accessing an invalid virtual address, confirming the race.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix race condition by disabling delayed work sync before cleanup of NTB bars in epf_ntb_epc_cleanup.
intent_record.what: Added a call to disable_delayed_work_sync(&ntb->cmd_handler) before the existing cleanup of memory windows, doorbell bars, and config bar in the epf_ntb_epc_cleanup function.
intent_record.how: This ensures that any pending or currently executing delayed work item (cmd_handler) is cancelled and synchronized before proceeding to clear the NTB bars, preventing potential race conditions where the work handler might access freed resources.

grouping_result.intent: Fix race condition by disabling delayed work sync before cleanup of NTB bars in epf_ntb_epc_cleanup.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by adding a delayed work sync before cleanup, preventing the use-after-free condition described in the root cause.
